• ••The Practical Help of Peter's Teaching••
	• Peter's teaching in 1 Peter 3:18-22 provides practical help for believers.
	• It encourages them to suffer in the will of God and glorify Christ.

Here are 10 bullets with sub-bullets summarizing the text:

â€¢ ••Christ's Death and Resurrection••
	• Christ died and yielded His spirit to the Father
	• He visited the realm of the dead and delivered a message to imprisoned spirits
	• The message was likely a declaration of victory over Satan and his hosts

â€¢ ••The Realm of the Dead••
	• The spirits in the realm of the dead were probably fallen angels
	• They were related to the pre-flood era and had a role in the wickedness of the world
	• The "sons of God" in Genesis 6:1-4 may have been fallen angels who cohabited with women

â€¢ ••The Resurrection of Christ••
	• Death involves the spirit leaving the body, and resurrection involves the spirit returning
	• The Father raised Jesus from the dead, but the Son also had authority to raise Himself
	• The resurrection of Christ is a miracle that declares His divinity and completes the work of salvation

â€¢ ••The Importance of the Resurrection••
	• The resurrection of Christ is essential to the gospel message
	• A dead Savior cannot save anyone, but the risen Christ gives us power for life and service
	• The resurrection of Christ declares that death has been conquered

â€¢ ••The Ascension of Christ••
	• Christ ascended to heaven 40 days after His resurrection
	• He sits at the right hand of the Father, the place of exaltation
	• Believers are seated with Him in the heavenlies and are able to "reign in life"

â€¢ ••Christ's Ministry••
	• Christ is ministering to the church as High Priest and Advocate
	• He is preparing a place for His people and will one day come to receive them to Himself
	• He has complete victory over all "angels and authorities and powers"

â€¢ ••The Ministry of Noah••
	• Noah was a "preacher of righteousness" during a difficult time in history
	• He was a hero of faith and was linked with Daniel and Job in Ezekiel 14:19-20
	• Peter saw a relationship between his readers and the ministry of Noah

â€¢ ••Noah's Ministry and the Gospel••
	• Noah's ministry was a call to righteousness in a wicked world
	• The gospel message is similar, calling people to righteousness and salvation
	• The ministry of Noah and the gospel message both emphasize the importance of faith and obedience

â€¢ ••Christ's Victory••
	• Christ's death, resurrection, and ascension declare His complete victory over Satan and his hosts
	• Believers do not fight for victory, but from victory, the mighty victory won by Christ

â€¢ ••The Significance of Christ's Ministry••
	• Christ's ministry is essential to our salvation and our daily lives
	• We are seated with Him in the heavenlies and are able to "reign in life"
	• Christ's ministry is a reminder of His complete victory over all evil powers.

Here are 10 bullets with sub-bullets summarizing the text:

â€¢ ••Noah's Faithfulness••
	• Noah preached God's truth for 120 years (Gen. 6:3)
	• He was laughed at and opposed, but remained faithful
	• His faithfulness is an encouragement to believers

â€¢ ••The Flood as a Picture of Baptism••
	• The flood pictures death, burial, and resurrection
	• Baptism is a picture of our Lord's death, burial, and resurrection
	• It symbolizes a clean break with the past and a commitment to Christ

â€¢ ••Baptism as a Consecration••
	• Candidates for baptism were interrogated carefully
	• Baptism was a serious matter in the early church
	• It was a step of consecration, not just an initiation rite

â€¢ ••The Ark as a Picture of Salvation••
	• The ark saved Noah and his family by faith
	• Sinners are saved by faith when they trust Christ and become one with Him

â€¢ ••Baptism and Salvation••
	• Baptism does not save us, but is a figure of salvation
	• The resurrection of Jesus Christ is what saves us (1 Peter 3:21)
	• Water cannot remove the stains of sin, only the blood of Christ can (1 John 1:7-2:2)

â€¢ ••Baptism and a Good Conscience••
	• A good conscience is important for a successful witness (1 Peter 3:16)
	• Baptism helps us have a good conscience by committing to Christ
	• A bad conscience can be a result of unfaithfulness to Christ

â€¢ ••The Word "Answer" in 1 Peter 3:21••
	• The word "answer" is a legal term meaning "a pledge, a demand"
	• When converts were prepared for baptism, they were asked to pledge to obey God and serve Him

â€¢ ••The Chronology of the Flood••
	• The flood's chronology is closely related to our Lord's day of resurrection
	• The ark rested on Ararat on the seventeenth day of the seventh month (Gen. 8:4)
	• This date corresponds to the date of our Lord's resurrection

â€¢ ••Our Lord's Experience on the Cross••
	• Our Lord's experience on the cross was a baptism of judgment
	• He referred to His sufferings as a baptism (Matt. 20:22; Luke 12:50)
	• He also used Jonah to illustrate His experience on the cross

â€¢ ••The Significance of the Flood••
	• The flood illustrates the importance of faithfulness and consecration
	• It pictures the death, burial, and resurrection of our Lord
	• It reminds us of the importance of having a good conscience and committing to Christ.

	• This word is used in the same way in the Gospel of John for the miracles of Jesus Christ

	• Symbolism is used to convey a deeper spiritual message than simply the display of power

â€¢ ••The Purpose of Symbolism••
	• Is not to confuse or obscure the meaning of the book

	• The book is a book of encouragement and hope for persecuted and suffering saints

Here are 10 bullets with sub-bullets summarizing the text:

••1. Symbolism in Revelation••
	• Symbols convey information, values, and emotions
	• John uses symbols to convey deeper spiritual truth
	• Examples: "Babylon the Great" and the "harlot" vs. the "bride"

••2. Understanding John's Symbolism••
	• Must be careful not to let imagination run wild
	• Biblical symbols are consistent with the whole of biblical revelation
	• Some symbols are explained, others are understood from Old Testament symbolism, and some are not explained at all

••3. The Readers of Revelation••
	• The book was originally sent to seven local churches in Asia Minor
	• God promised a special blessing to those who read and obey the message
	• The verb "read" means "to read out loud", indicating the book was first read aloud in local church meetings

••4. Purpose of the Book••
	• Not to satisfy curiosity about the future
	• To give encouragement and strength to God's people during intense persecution
	• To help them examine their own lives and correct areas needing improvement

••5. The Number Seven in Revelation••
	• Signifies fullness and completeness
	• Examples: seven seals, seven trumpets, seven vials, seven stars, and seven lampstands

••6. The Seven Churches••
	• Each church received a special message from Christ
	• Some students see the seven churches as a "panorama of church history"
	• The letters remind us that the exalted Head of the church knows what's going on in each assembly

••7. The Importance of Relationship with Christ••
	• The churches in Asia Minor were facing persecution and needed to be rightly related to the Lord and to each other
	• They are pictured as seven separate lampstands, each giving light in a dark world

••8. The Need for Correction••
	• At least five of the assemblies required correction if their lights were to shine brightly
	• The Lord reminded them of who He is and encouraged them to be "overcomers"

••9. The Blessing of Reading and Obedience••
	• The blessing comes not just by hearing, but by doing
	• See James 1:22-25 for more on this

••10. The Seven Beatitudes in Revelation••
	• Examples: 1:3; 14:13; 16:15; 19:9; 20:6; 22:7, 14
	• The number seven is significant in Revelation, signifying fullness and completeness.

	• Satan's name means "accuser" and he stands at the throne of God, fighting the saints by accusing them (Job 1-2; Zech. 3).

â€¢ ••Jesus Christ's Representation••
	• Jesus Christ is the "heavenly Advocate" who represents the church before God's holy throne (1 John 2:1-2).

â€¢ ••Satan's Deception••

â€¢ ••The Church's Response••
	• The church can always defeat the enemy by being faithful to Jesus Christ.
	• The church's witness to God's Word and willingness to lay down their lives for Christ defeats Satan.

â€¢ ••Satan's Power••
	• Satan's power is limited and his tactics must fail when God's people trust the power of the blood and the Word.
	• Satan is not equal to God; he is not omnipotent, omnipresent, or omniscient.

â€¢ ••The Church's Victory in Heaven••
	• The church will come forth in glory without spot or wrinkle, or any such thing (Eph. 5:24-27).
	• Satan will become angry and threaten the peace of heaven when he sees his tactics have failed.

â€¢ ••Satan's Wrath on Earth••
	• Satan will vent his anger on earth, particularly against Israel (the woman).
	• Satan creates a wave of anti-Semitism, trying to destroy the nation and prevent the Messiah's return.

â€¢ ••The Remnant's Escape••
	• A Jewish remnant must be ready to receive the Messiah and form the nucleus for the kingdom (Zech. 12:9-14:21; Rev. 1:7).
	• God will prepare a special place to protect and care for the Jewish remnant.

Here are 10 bullets with sub-bullets summarizing the text:

••1. The City of God••
• The City of God is the New Jerusalem, the eternal home prepared for the Lamb's wife (Rev. 21:9ff.)
• Each generation of believers must keep itself pure from the pollution of both the "harlot" and "Babylon"

••2. The Desolation of the Harlot••
• The scene begins with an invitation from an angel to John to come and see what God will do with the "beast's" worldwide religious system (Rev. 17:1-2)
• The woman is called a "harlot" four times in this chapter, and her sin is called "fornication" (Rev. 17:2, 4)

••3. The Description of the Harlot••
• The woman is dressed in expensive garments, decorated with gold and precious stones (Rev. 17:4)
• She is holding a golden cup in her hand and is drunk with the blood of the saints (Rev. 17:6)
• She is seated upon "many waters" and upon a scarlet beast with seven heads and ten horns (Rev. 17:1)

••4. The Meaning of the Symbols••
• The angel explains the symbols to John and all believers (Rev. 17:7-18)
• The woman is identified with a city that existed in John's day, which is prosperous and powerful but also idolatrous and dangerous (Rev. 17:18)

••5. The City of Babylon••
• The city of Babylon was founded by Nimrod (Gen. 10:8-11)
• The name Babylon means "the gate of God," but it has come to mean "confusion" due to the idolatrous attempt by man to defy God (Gen. 11:1-9)

••6. The Babylonian Influence••
• The Babylonian system has given birth to all false religions and has seduced men into opposing God and persecuting His servants
• The Babylonian influence has been felt throughout history, from the beginning of Nimrod's city in Genesis 10

••7. The Seven Mountains••
• The seven mountains probably symbolize the city of Rome, built on seven hills (Rev. 17:9)
• The Roman Empire was living in luxury, spreading false religion, polluting the nations with its idolatry and sin, and persecuting the church

••8. The Scarlet Beast••
• The scarlet beast is a symbol of Satan and sin (Rev. 12:3, Isa. 1:18)
• The beast has seven heads and ten horns, representing the worldwide power and influence of the harlot

••9. The Harlot's Sin••
• The harlot's sin is called "fornication" and involves polluting the nations with its filth and abomination (Rev. 17:2, 4)
• She persecutes those who belong to the Lord and is drunk with the blood of the saints (Rev. 17:6)

••10. The Mystery of Babylon••
• The mystery of Babylon is a hidden truth that only the spiritually initiated can understand (Rev. 17:5)
• The mystery has to do with the Babylonian system and its influence on the world, which has given birth to all false religions and has seduced men into opposing God.

	• The church, the bride of the Lamb, is the habitation of God, while Babylon is the habitation of Satan.

	• The sin of Babylon is that of "fornication" or idolatry.
	• The system has polluted the whole world with its riches and pleasures.
• ••The Warning to Christians••
	• Christians must beware of the subtle influence of the world system.
	• We must not become fascinated by the things the world has to offer, but rather love God above all else.
• ••The World System••
	• The world system opposes Christ and has always been with us.
	• We must be aware of its influence and beware of its subtle temptations.

	• Satan's counterfeit religion is subtle and requires spiritual discernment to recognize.
	• We must be careful not to be seduced away from our sincere devotion to Christ.

	• In these last days, we all need to heed the admonitions in 1 Timothy 4 and 2 Timothy 3.
	• We must remain true to our Lord and not conform to "popular religion".

â€¢ ••John's Second Vision and Counsel••
	• John was overwhelmed by what he saw and heard
	• The angel gave John three words of counsel:
		- Do not worship angels
		- Worship God
		- Do not seal up the Revelation

â€¢ ••The Living Unity of God's Word••
	• Scripture is its own best interpreter
	• John used Old Testament images and prophecies in his writing

â€¢ ••The Warning of Revelation 22:11••
	• Decision determines character
	• Character determines destiny
	• Suffering believers should continue to live a godly life

â€¢ ••The Responsibility of Serving the Lord••
	• God is mindful of our sufferings and service
	• Nothing will be done in vain if it is done for Him
	• Believers will be judged according to their works at the judgment seat of Christ

â€¢ ••The Importance of Faithfulness••
	• Believers should not become careless and lazy just because Jesus is coming soon
	• Paul faced this problem with some believers in Thessalonica
	• We should watch and be faithful if we really believe Jesus is coming soon

â€¢ ••The Encouragement of Revelation 22:13••
	• Whatever God starts, He will finish
	• He is the Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the ending, the first and the last

â€¢ ••The Importance of Keeping Our Lives Clean••
	• Obedience to God's Word is a mark of true salvation
	• Those who do God's commandments will enter the city, while those who reject His Word will be excluded

â€¢ ••The Significance of Jesus' Titles••
	• The "root" speaks of humility, while the "star" speaks of majesty and glory
	• The "root and offspring of David" speaks of Jesus' Jewish, national name
	• The "bright and morning star" speaks of Jesus' universal name

â€¢ ••The Coming of Jesus Christ••
	• Jesus will come quickly, and men will not have time to change their characters
	• Jesus will reward those who have been faithful and obedient to His Word

Here are 10 bullets with sub-bullets summarizing the text:

• ••The Return of Jesus••
	• Jesus will return as the "Sun of righteousness" in burning fury (Mal. 4:1-3)
	• God's people look for His return and keep their lives clean and dedicated to Him (1 John 2:28-3:3)
• ••The Importance of Expecting Jesus' Return••
	• We must keep expecting Jesus Christ to return (Rev. 22:7, 12, 20)
	• The Spirit of God, through the church, calls for Jesus to come (Rev. 22:20)
• ••The Delay of Jesus' Return••
	• Jesus has delayed His return for nearly 2,000 years
	• God wants to give this sinful world opportunity to repent and be saved (2 Peter 3:1ff.)
• ••The Church's Role in Expecting Jesus' Return••
	• The church (the bride) calls for Jesus to come (Rev. 22:20)
	• Believers should invite lost sinners to trust Christ and drink the water of life
• ••The Motivation of Bible Prophecy••
	• A true understanding of Bible prophecy should motivate us to obey God's Word
	• It should also motivate us to share God's invitation with a lost world
• ••The Call to Ministry and Evangelism••
	• When the church lives in expectancy of Christ's return, it provokes ministry and evangelism
	• It also leads to purity of heart and a desire to tell others of God's grace
• ••The Invitation to Come, Lord Jesus••
	• The Bible's last prayer is "Even so, come, Lord Jesus" (Rev. 22:20)
	• We should join John in this prayer and invite Jesus to come
• ••Being Ready for Jesus' Return••
	• We should be ready for Jesus' return, both individually and as a church
	• We should be living in obedience to God's Word and sharing His invitation with others
• ••The Role of the Spirit in Expecting Jesus' Return••
	• The Spirit of God, through the church, calls for Jesus to come (Rev. 22:20)
	• The Spirit leads us to understand and obey God's Word
• ••The Importance of Sharing God's Invitation••
	• We should invite lost sinners to trust Christ and drink the water of life
	• We should share God's invitation with a lost world, motivated by a true understanding of Bible prophecy
